profile.headline: Systems/Software Engineer II @ Hewlett Packard Enterprise

positions.title: Automation Specialist I
positions.description:
Programmed and implemented PLC and HMI software for critical equipment at major pharmaceutical clients to conform with regulatory standards and expand automation capabilities. 
Developed and executed Installation and Operational Qualification protocols to validate functionality and 
conformance of PLC, physical IOs, HMI, interlocks and machine operation. 
Configured and documented clients’ automated and periodic backups for disaster recovery of key machine files within secure internal network. 
Owned project scope and schedule from kickoff to closing; regularly presented metrics to clients and stakeholders.
positions.insights: Automation, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and +3 skills

positions.title: Applications Engineer
positions.locationName: Sugar Land, Texas, United States · On-site
positions.description:
Designed and executed validation testing for clocking, camera, and memory interfaces of automotive processors at worst-case performance and environmental conditions to ensure regulatory compliance of new devices. 
Developed modular automation suites (C code, LabVIEW, TestStand) for industrial microprocessors to sample tunable voltages, currents and ADC parameters and compare them against spec values, reducing turnaround at key device milestones and giving new devices a framework to branch from as needed. 
Characterized previously-untested spread spectrum clocking functionality on existing device by generating 
comprehensive dataset and technical analysis to enable major customer’s reduction of electromagnetic emissions in their system. 
Implemented and expanded tools to automate creation of data-sheet specifications, system configuration code, and power estimates for new devices. 
Published and maintained first version of customer tool which enabled automated creation of starter-code based on custom use cases to increase ease of use. 
Investigated root cause of system failures on customer boards for camera and memory interfaces and made direct recommendations for performance issues via online forum. 
Interfaced with high-end oscilloscopes, function generators, thermal systems, power supplies, and performed test board modifications to collect precise data.
positions.insights: Hardware Development, Embedded C and +12 skills

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.locationName: Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States · On-site
positions.description:
Designed control algorithm in MATLAB to simulate power flow of residential microgrids for
optimal cost, emissions, and robustness
Integrated support for solar energy under variable weather conditions, energy storage, and
charging/discharging of hybrid vehicle at desirable times based on user-defined goals.
Participated actively in regular meetings with fellow researchers to discuss project updates,
challenges faced, and lessons learned during ongoing activities.

company.name: University of Michigan Undergraduate Research Opportunity Program

educations.schoolName: University of Michigan College of Engineering

projects.title: Medlaunch - Sleep Aid Device, Stroke Rehabilitation Device
projects.description:
Led hardware group to create sleep aid device intended to identify and respond to sleep stages; identified optimal microcontroller, biosensors, battery sizing and communication protocol
Implemented sensor fusion algorithms for wearable IMU to track arm orientation/position for aid in physical rehabilitation
Performed outreach with community partners and professionals to determine precise technical, economic, and ergonomic design constraints

projects.title: VLSI RISC Microprocessor Design (Capstone Project)
projects.description:
Designed RISC microprocessor hierarchically at the transistor level, accounting for power, area and delay by 
optimizing employed logic, sizing, layout and routing
Satisfied process spacing requirements for 16-bit register file, ALU, and bit shifter using both hand layout and 
logic synthesis tools
